using MPI
using CUDA
using JSON3

# JACC.parallel_for(dims, f, x...) calls f(i, x...) per index. f must be a
# named function, so it is defined here and not inside a try block.
# The backend must be CUDA. JACC 1.3.1 reads its backend from Preferences,
# not from the environment, so an ENV variable here would do nothing. A
# JACC run on the threads backend returns the same numbers as a run on the
# GPU, so the numbers alone cannot tell the two apart. This check compares
# the array type instead, which differs.
#
# Set the preference once, on the login node, in the default environment
# and with no project flag:
#   julia -e 'import JACC; JACC.set_backend(:cuda)'
# Preferences are read when a package loads, so the change takes effect on
# the next job.
function jacc_backend_info()
    d = Dict{String,Any}()
    d["array_type"] = try string(JACC.array_type()) catch e; "unavailable" end
    d["backend"]    = try string(JACC.default_backend()) catch e; "unavailable" end
    at = try string(typeof(JACC.array(Float32[1, 2]))) catch e; "unavailable" end
    d["sample_array_type"] = at
    # "unavailable" means the accessor threw. That is a failure, not a
    # device array, so it must not read as on_device.
    d["on_device"] = at != "unavailable" && !startswith(at, "Vector") && !startswith(at, "Array")
    return d
end

function jacc_vadd_i(i, y, a, b)
    y[i] = a[i] + b[i]
end

MPI.Init()
comm   = MPI.COMM_WORLD
rank   = MPI.Comm_rank(comm)
nranks = MPI.Comm_size(comm)

# Node-local communicator. The rank index inside it is the only correct
# key for selecting a GPU: MPI.COMM_WORLD's rank index counts across
# nodes, so rank 2 on node B would pick device 2, which does not exist.
local_comm = MPI.Comm_split_type(comm, MPI.COMM_TYPE_SHARED, 0)
local_rank = MPI.Comm_rank(local_comm)
local_size = MPI.Comm_size(local_comm)

r = Dict{String,Any}()
r["hostname"]   = gethostname()
r["rank"]       = rank
r["nranks"]     = nranks
r["local_rank"] = local_rank
r["local_size"] = local_size

# This topology must give 4 ranks on 2 nodes. Fewer means the job did not
# run the template this check expects. The usual cause is a poller.sh on
# the login node that has no entry for "multi_node_multi_gpu", which makes
# it fall back to the single-GPU template. Without this test the run would
# skip every transfer below and report no error, which reads as a pass.
if nranks < 4
    r["error"] = "expected 4 ranks, got $nranks. Check that poller.sh on the login node maps multi_node_multi_gpu to run_job_multi_node_multi_gpu_a30.sbatch"
end
if local_size < 2
    r["error"] = "expected 2 ranks per node, got $local_size on $(gethostname())"
end

# Node identity and CUDA versions, before any kernel launch. A SIGSEGV is
# not catchable and destroys the result JSON, so these also go to stderr,
# which Slurm keeps.
# Each field goes in its own try. One unavailable accessor must not cost
# the others, because these fields are the evidence for which GPU a rank
# holds.
probe!(d, k, f) = try d[k] = f() catch e; d[k] = "unavailable" end

try
    r["ndevices"] = CUDA.ndevices()
    CUDA.device!(local_rank % CUDA.ndevices())
catch e
    r["device_error"] = sprint(showerror, e)
end
probe!(r, "device",   () -> string(CUDA.device()))
probe!(r, "gpu_name", () -> CUDA.name(CUDA.device()))
probe!(r, "driver",   () -> string(CUDA.driver_version()))
probe!(r, "runtime",  () -> string(CUDA.runtime_version()))
probe!(r, "uuid",     () -> string(CUDA.uuid(CUDA.device())))
println(stderr, "NODE: ", r)
flush(stderr)

# --- (a) intra-node, GPU to GPU -------------------------------------
intra = Dict{String,Any}()
try
    if local_size < 2
        intra["skipped"] = "only $local_size rank on this node"
    else
        buf = CUDA.fill(Float32(100 + rank), 4)
        if local_rank == 0
            MPI.Send(buf, local_comm; dest=1, tag=10)
            intra["sent"] = 100 + rank
        elseif local_rank == 1
            MPI.Recv!(buf, local_comm; source=0, tag=10)
            intra["received"] = Array(buf)
        end
    end
catch e
    intra["error"] = sprint(showerror, e)
end
r["intra_node"] = intra

# --- (b) inter-node --------------------------------------------------
# One communicator holding the local-rank-0 process of every node.
# Leaders are found with an Allgather over MPI.COMM_WORLD rather than a
# second Comm_split. Every rank then learns which world ranks are leaders,
# and the transfer runs on MPI.COMM_WORLD. This needs one MPI call whose
# signature is already used elsewhere in the suite.
inter = Dict{String,Any}()
try
    all_local = MPI.Allgather(local_rank, comm)
    leaders   = [i - 1 for i in 1:length(all_local) if all_local[i] == 0]
    inter["leaders"] = leaders
    if length(leaders) < 2
        inter["skipped"] = "only $(length(leaders)) node"
    elseif rank == leaders[1]
        buf = CUDA.fill(Float32(200 + rank), 4)
        MPI.Send(buf, comm; dest=leaders[2], tag=20)
        inter["sent"] = 200 + rank
    elseif rank == leaders[2]
        buf = CUDA.fill(Float32(200 + rank), 4)
        MPI.Recv!(buf, comm; source=leaders[1], tag=20)
        inter["received"] = Array(buf)
        inter["expected"] = 200 + leaders[1]
    else
        inter["skipped"] = "not a node leader"
    end
catch e
    inter["error"] = sprint(showerror, e)
end
r["inter_node"] = inter

# --- (c) global Allreduce over all ranks -----------------------------
# Every rank contributes rank+1. The sum over 4 ranks is 1+2+3+4 = 10.
# This is the only check in the suite that runs a collective, and a
# reduction is what a data-parallel gradient sum depends on.
allred = Dict{String,Any}()
try
    buf = CUDA.fill(Float32(rank + 1), 4)
    MPI.Allreduce!(buf, +, comm)
    got = Array(buf)
    want = Float32(div(nranks * (nranks + 1), 2))
    allred["result"]   = got
    allred["expected"] = want
    allred["ok"]       = all(got .== want)
catch e
    allred["error"] = sprint(showerror, e)
end
r["allreduce"] = allred

# --- (d) JACC.jl on this rank's own GPU ------------------------------
# JACC follows the CUDA device selected above, so this runs on the same
# GPU as the transfers. Four ranks therefore cover four distinct A30s.
#
# The import must be its own completed top-level statement before any
# code that uses a JACC macro. Julia macro-expands a whole top-level
# block before it runs any of it, so `import JACC` and
# `JACC.@init_backend` cannot share one try block.
a_host = Float32[1, 2, 3, 4]
b_host = Float32[10, 20, 30, 40]
n = length(a_host)

try
    import JACC
catch e
    r["jacc"] = Dict("error" => "import JACC failed: $(sprint(showerror, e))")
end
if !haskey(r, "jacc")
    try
        a_j = JACC.array(a_host)
        b_j = JACC.array(b_host)
        y_j = JACC.zeros(Float32, n)
        JACC.parallel_for(n, jacc_vadd_i, y_j, a_j, b_j)
        JACC.synchronize()
        info = jacc_backend_info()
        info["result"] = Array(y_j)
        if !info["on_device"]
            info["error"] = "JACC ran on the host. array_type is $(info["sample_array_type"]). " *
                            "Run `julia -e 'import JACC; JACC.set_backend(:cuda)'` once on the " *
                            "login node, in the default environment, with no project flag. " *
                            "A JACC result computed on the host says nothing about the GPU."
        end
        r["jacc"] = info
    catch e
        r["jacc"] = Dict("error" => sprint(showerror, e))
    end
end

# --- (e) Allreduce over a JACC array ---------------------------------
# MPI.Allreduce! needs the underlying device array. Whether a JACC array
# is already one depends on the backend JACC selects at run time. This
# test answers the question instead of assuming it. It tries the JACC
# array first, then its parent, and records which path worked.
# The body lives in a function on purpose. At top level a try block opens
# a soft scope, so `buf = ...` inside the fallback catch would create a
# local and leave the outer buf untouched. The result read after the try
# would then come from the buffer the fallback never wrote. Inside a
# function the reassignment behaves as written.
#
# Every rank takes the same branch, because every rank builds the same
# JACC array type. A run where one rank falls back and another does not
# would hang, since the two would call different collectives.
function jacc_allreduce_test(rank, nranks, n, comm)
    d = Dict{String,Any}()
    want = Float32(div(nranks * (nranks + 1), 2))
    d["expected"]   = want
    d["array_type"] = string(typeof(JACC.array(Float32[1.0])))
    buf  = JACC.array(fill(Float32(rank + 1), n))
    path = "direct"
    try
        MPI.Allreduce!(buf, +, comm)
    catch e1
        d["direct_error"] = sprint(showerror, e1)
        buf  = JACC.array(fill(Float32(rank + 1), n))
        MPI.Allreduce!(parent(buf), +, comm)
        path = "parent"
    end
    got = Array(buf)
    d["path"]   = path
    d["result"] = got
    d["ok"]     = all(got .== want)
    return d
end

if haskey(r, "jacc") && !haskey(r["jacc"], "error")
    try
        r["jacc_mpi"] = jacc_allreduce_test(rank, nranks, n, comm)
    catch e
        r["jacc_mpi"] = Dict("error" => sprint(showerror, e))
    end
else
    r["jacc_mpi"] = Dict("skipped" => "JACC unavailable on this rank")
end

# --- gather onto rank 0 ----------------------------------------------
# Only rank 0 prints. mpirun merges every rank's stdout into one stream,
# so any other rank printing would corrupt the result line.
if rank == 0
    final = Dict{String,Any}("rank0" => r)
    for src in 1:(nranks - 1)
        try
            final["rank$(src)"] = MPI.recv(comm; source=src, tag=1)
        catch e
            final["rank$(src)"] = Dict("error" => "no payload from rank $src: $(sprint(showerror, e))")
        end
    end

    # Two ranks on one node must hold two different GPUs. Compare by UUID
    # when the driver supplies one, and by device index otherwise. An
    # index comparison is only meaningful when a rank sees every GPU on
    # its node: if Slurm binds one GPU per task, both ranks see index 0
    # while holding different physical GPUs.
    byhost = Dict{String,Vector{Any}}()
    for k in keys(final)
        e = final[k]
        h = get(e, "hostname", "?")
        push!(get!(byhost, h, Any[]), e)
    end
    dist = Dict{String,Any}()
    for (h, es) in byhost
        uu = [get(e, "uuid", "unavailable") for e in es]
        ids = [get(e, "device", "?") for e in es]
        nd  = [get(e, "ndevices", 0) for e in es]
        if length(es) < 2
            dist[h] = Dict("ranks" => length(es), "verdict" => "one rank on this node")
        elseif all(u -> u != "unavailable", uu)
            dist[h] = Dict("ranks" => length(es), "uuids" => uu,
                           "distinct" => length(unique(uu)) == length(uu),
                           "basis" => "uuid")
        elseif all(n -> n >= length(es), nd)
            dist[h] = Dict("ranks" => length(es), "devices" => ids,
                           "distinct" => length(unique(ids)) == length(ids),
                           "basis" => "device index")
        else
            dist[h] = Dict("ranks" => length(es), "devices" => ids, "ndevices" => nd,
                           "distinct" => "unknown",
                           "basis" => "one GPU visible per task, index cannot decide")
        end
    end
    final["gpu_distinct_per_node"] = dist
    println(JSON3.write(final))
else
    MPI.send(r, comm; dest=0, tag=1)
end
